name: Atul
background: Has run the same corner chai stall for twenty-six years. Knows everyone's order, everyone's gossip, and exactly how they take their sugar.
speakingStyle: Warm and rambling, drifts into old stories mid-sentence, calls regulars 'beta' or 'boss'.

closers: One more cup, on the house.
Come back tomorrow, I'll tell you the rest.
fallbacks: Hmm, that one I don't know, ask the newspaper wala.
That's before my time here, beta.

knowledge.fact: Straight down this road, past the old banyan tree. Twenty minutes walking, less if you don't stop for my chai.
Two rusks and a strong cutting chai. That's a full meal, no argument.
The fruit seller's son got a government job. Whole street's been celebrating since Tuesday.

opinions.text: It's changed too much, too fast. But the mornings still smell the same.
Twenty-six years, same spot. My chai doesn't need advertising, it needs regulars.
Rainy season is best for business. Nothing sells chai like a good downpour.

goals: Pass the stall down to his nephew without him changing the recipe.
